Agents swept 131 Awwwards award rows — Sites of the Year and Sites of the Month, from 2018 through June 2026 — opened each one, and wrote down what it actually does. Then they compiled it into a skill, and tested whether the skill makes better pages. It did not, at first.

Every figure about the dataset is generated from it; design constants are cited beside what they drive; figures quoted from the dated decision log carry their date.

  1. Harvest131 award rowsCrawl the archives. Rows kept at 2018+, each with its award, date and live URL.

  5. Validate2,289 → 1,118 findingsEvery constant re-checked for whether it takes effect — not just whether it was copied correctly.
  6. Compile730 constantsThe survivors became a skill an agent designs from, citing each value by record ID.

The web forgets its winners

Every studied site, by the year it first won, tinted with its recorded palette — the site's declared tokens where its build exposes them, screenshot-sampled for 22 (dotted frames). A struck frame is a site whose awarded design is gone, even where the domain still answers. 70% of 2018–19 winners are offline; 11% of 2023 onward.

  1. (1)2026-08-14

    The acceptance gate checked that every citation existed, not that it was useful. Both test briefs passed while citing a priors file in which 1% of lines carried a usable constant.

    A gate that checks existence and not substance will pass a hollow artifact.

  2. (2)2026-08-14

    The first version of this page read its family's "stock easings only" as "no motion" and shipped a static document. Rejected: "no hint of awwwards at all."

    The skill now carries a motion budget per family: a strict curve set is never a small budget.

  3. (3)2026-09-24

    The skill's own instructions — in the paragraph telling agents never to type provenance numbers — said 32% of 2018–19 winners were offline. That was the archive-wide rate. Counted from the cards, it is 70%.

    A number typed beside a rule against typing numbers is still typed.

Kiln & Quire

A two-person letterpress and risograph print studio in Kyoto that sells limited-edition prints and runs weekend workshops. Page: landing page — hero plus ONE scroll section introducing the weekend workshop. Audience: design-literate tourists and locals. The owners hate "zen minimalism" clichés.

V1 · 2026-09-23 skill 44 · base 48 0 of 1 verdict · baseline wins
V2 · 2026-09-24 skill 47.7 · base 47.5 2 of 3 verdicts · tie on means (Δ+0.2)
Baselinesame file: 48 → 47.5judge drift

Gale

An open-source time-series database built for wind-farm telemetry (millions of turbine sensor readings per second). Page: launch landing page — hero plus ONE section explaining ingest speed. Audience: infrastructure engineers. It must not look like every other dev-tool site.

V1 · 2026-09-23 skill 44 · base 46 0 of 1 verdict · baseline wins
V2 · 2026-09-24 skill 51.5 · base 40.8 3 of 3 verdicts · skill wins
Baselinesame file: 46 → 40.8judge drift

Read with care. Two briefs, one build each; judges differ between runs, and the same baseline file scored differently (the drift rows above). This is evidence the rebuild helped, not proof.
